subject: Proposal: capacity stitch + utilization sweep for HelixAI renewal
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Helix renewal — plan for sizing 

Team —

Quick internal note before we send anything official to Helix. Their renewal conversation is shifting from a flat tranche add to a more surgical approach: we should propose a short "utilization sweep" to reconcile actual 90-day peak profiles and then stitch a capacity proposal to avoid over-provisioning. Goals: protect their SLA during peak windows, reduce idle slots during off-peak, and present a clear, time-bound SOW for a staged add (30% burst pool + scheduled hotstandby).

I ran a coarse model against the usage export Ben pulled last night — putting it in capacity_model_v3.xlsx. Highlights:
- Sustained 7-day rolling mean is only ~65% of their committed slot baseline during non-peak windows.
- Short spikes (1–3 hours) push utilization >95% on a subset of GPU pools during ETL / retraining jobs.
- Opportunity: short-duration burst credits + a small hot-standby cushion will knock expected monthly spend down ~12% vs full tranche add while meeting latency SLOs.

Action items for this morning:
1) Ben: sketch the SOW language for a 60-day utilization sweep + staged 3-week burst ramp. Attach to the external email as SOW_HelixAI_draft.pdf.
2) David: verify that Dedicated infra can schedule a hot-standby pool with the routing fallback we described (model variant fallback + KV cache priming) and surface any lead time constraints.
3) Marissa: prepare a short one-page executive summary for Anna that frames cost + risk tradeoffs.

I will draft the outbound note once we have Ben's SOW and David's gating notes. Keep replies succinct here — we'll iterate quickly and send to Anna this afternoon.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_model_v3.xlsx (summary workbook)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Ruiz <anna@helix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 14:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: utilization sweep + staged capacity add (Helix renewal)

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last week. Per our discussion I wanted to propose a lower-risk approach to handling your upcoming seasonal spike: a short utilization validation period followed by a staged capacity "stitch" rather than a full tranche purchase up front. The goal is to keep your tail latency and throughput predictable while minimizing idle monthly spend.

What we're proposing (high level):
- 60-day utilization sweep: Redwood will run a tuned sampling and workload-aware batching analysis over a representative 60-day window to validate peak contours. We will collect and analyze per-model request latency/seq-length distributions and KV cache hit patterns.
- Staged capacity stitch: after the sweep, we propose a 3-week staged add: 30% burst pool (pre-warmed GPUs with rapid autoscale) + a 10% hot-standby cushion for canary fallback. If the sweep shows higher-than-expected tails, we convert an agreed portion of the burst pool to committed slots with a 30-day notice.
- Economics: modeled outcome (attached) shows ~12% lower monthly unit cost vs a full tranche add while preserving 99th percentile latency targets for your production routes.

I've attached a short summary (capacity_model_v3.xlsx) and a draft SOW (SOW_HelixAI_draft.pdf) to make timing and responsibilities clear. Ben is copied and will pull contract language once you sign off on the approach.

If this is reasonable, can you:
1) Confirm you can share the 90-day raw trace (or the ops export we requested) by end of week so David can kick off a gating review.
2) Confirm whether Finance needs a formal quote now or if a provisional quote is fine pending the sweep.

Open to a 20-minute sync tomorrow afternoon if you'd like to run through the tradeoffs.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_model_v3.xlsx; SOW_HelixAI_draft.pdf

From: Anna Ruiz <anna@helix.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: utilization sweep + staged capacity add (Helix renewal)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear plan. We like the staged approach; it reduces upfront spend and gives our platform team confidence. I'm attaching a sanitized ops export (helix_usage_export_202608.csv) — it contains per-hour slot utilization and job tags; we've stripped PII.

Two quick questions before we commit:
1) During the 60-day sweep, will we pay at peak committed rates or at an evaluative rate? We prefer not to trigger committed billing until we convert the burst pool.
2) Can the hot-standby cushion be reserved per-region? We run heavier inference in us-west but have important failover paths in eu-central.

I'll also pull finance into the thread if we move forward.

Anna Ruiz
Head of Platform
HelixAI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Helix renewal — SOW + provisioning cadence

Kim / team —

Thanks — Anna confirmed she'll send the 90-day export (attached) and asked the two questions below. Drafted answers and next steps:

Q1 (billing during sweep): We bill at an evaluative, non-committed rate for any burst capacity consumed during the 60-day sweep; committed billing only triggers if Helix signs to convert burst pool portions to committed slots (we'll include a 30-day conversion clause). I'll put the exact rate table into the SOW.

Q2 (regional hot-standby): We can reserve the hot-standby cushion per-region; however, eu-central reservations require a 10-business-day lead time for dedicated allocation versus us-west which is 3 business days. David — confirm scheduling steps and whether autoscale warmup (KV cache priming) will need additional time for region hops.

Planned schedule (provisional):
- Week 0: Helix delivers 90-day export. Redwood onboarding + infra gating check (David).
- Weeks 1–2: 60-day sweep runs (sampling + targeted instrumentation).
- Week 3: Results review + decision point; if convert, 30-day clock to make part of burst pool committed.
- Weeks 4–6: Staged 3-week ramp for burst + hot-standby activation.

I've attached an updated SOW (SOW_HelixAI_draft.pdf) with the billing table placeholder and included the Drive link to the capacity model. Please review and I'll send to Anna once David confirms the lead time note.

Ben Carter
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_HelixAI_draft.pdf
Related link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/helix-capacity-model-v3
